newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open softer, awaiting Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open softer, awaiting Greenspan.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened softer on Tuesday as jittery investors awaited testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on the state of the U.S. economy and markets.

"It's just the tone of the market that we're going to see ahead of Humphrey-Hawkins testimony," one money market trader said. Greenspan is scheduled to address the House Banking subcommittee of the U.S. Congress today and tomorrow.
Canada's three-month cash T-bill traded to yield 3.35 percent from 3.33 percent at Monday's close.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill weakened to yield 3.75 percent from a 3.71 percent on Monday. The one-year when-issued T-bill eased to yield 4.22 percent from 4.20 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.25 percent, in the middle of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.

Canadian T-bills traded softer on Tuesday as the currency weakened overnight to open at C$1.3804 (US$0.7244) from Monday's close of C$1.3772 (US$0.7261), prompting worries that the Bank of Canada may soon hike short-term interest rates, traders said.

"There's some renewed discussion about the bank," one trader said. The Bank of Canada last month surprised markets by hiking rates 25 basis points to boost buying in the Canadian dollar, its first tightening in more than two years.
Trading flows were thin and likely to remain so ahead of Greenspan's 1400 EDT/1800 GMT start, one trader said. "It's simply a matter of wait and see."
